items.title: J. Leo Rayhill interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 23, 2007
items.q: I remember being in Tommy Joy’s a number of times, I practically lived there with Joe Sullivan.

ctx.x: Let me take you back. We’re going to talk about your show a little more, but I’m curious about Utica in the 1940s and sort of this jazz club scene in your high school. What was the racial relations like back then?
It was pretty good. Because they had, I remember being in Tommy Joy’s a number of times, I practically lived there with Joe Sullivan. Remember Joe Sullivan?
